name: research-review
description: Chained research review: review:{key} -> verify:{key} -> why:{key} -> brainstorm:{key} -> refute:{key} over args.targets [{key,hypothesis,experiments,files,focus,verdict}]. Stage 3 mints the WHY idea under the hypothesis when the round was disproved or inconclusive (else writes push_further); stage 4 mints 1-5 hypotheses under that idea; stage 5 keeps/modifies/drops them into a ready_batch. Every later stage receives the earlier stage's structured return through chained_from placeholders only -- no director-authored glue. Authored by kid a00-cc347774 (TM.60) for hypothesis:lm-chained-research-review-cuts-director-glue-calls, following goal:g14. NOTE: workflow.py author cannot yet generate a 5-stage chained script, so both halves were authored by hand; the manifest is the source and agi-research-review.js is derived from it by the same conventions. The mint gate: run args `mint` (default ABSENT = false) gates the real write.py create calls in stages 3 and 4; a bare run is PROPOSE-ONLY and always fills proposed_idea_title/body and proposed_hypotheses, while `mint: true` mints as before.

stages.label: review
stages.prompt:
You are reviewing ONE research round on the agi graph (READ-ONLY: never edit, commit, or touch tmux/systemd/crontab). Target {key}: hypothesis node {hypothesis}; experiment nodes: {experiments}; files in scope: {files}; focus: {focus}. Node files live under .agi/nodes/<type>/<slug>.md (frontmatter + body). Rules: MECHANISM not wording, cite file:line or node:field for every judgement; a claim about a reader that was never read is wording; a green test can require a defect; a test that touches a REAL tmux pane, systemd unit, crontab or process is a defect. You MAY run single COMMITTED test files with `cd {project_root} && env -u TMUX -u TMUX_PANE python3 -m pytest extensions/agi/tests/<file> -q -p no:cacheprovider`. NEVER author a probe that calls rotate/heal/send/dispatch functions. Return ONLY the structured result.

Steps: (1) read the hypothesis testable_claim and split it into conjuncts; (2) read each experiment node: verdict, evidence_runs (a decisive verdict needs >=1 and evidence_runs must resolve to real nodes; an experiment may cite itself, a verdict may not), parents; (3) for every conjunct find the mechanism in the named bytes and cite file:line, status MET / NOT_MET / UNVERIFIED; (4) run the round's test files individually if any and report counts; (5) check no test or code path reaches a real pane, unit, crontab or process; (6) state any step only the PRIME can do, with exact commands and what proves it; (7) recommend accept / demote / accept_with_residue and list every defect with severity demote|residue|note. defects_summary must be a plain-text numbered list `title -- file:line -- detail`, or the word NONE. Budget: at most 12 tool calls; read only the named nodes and files, do not explore the wider graph.

RETURN CONTRACT: return ONE flat JSON object (a ```json fence is fine) whose TOP-LEVEL keys are exactly: round (string, the target key, = "{key}"), verdict_recommendation (accept|demote|accept_with_residue), conjuncts (array of {claim,status,evidence}), defects (array of {title,file,detail,severity}), defects_summary (string), tests_run (string), node_checks (string), prime_step (string). Do NOT nest them under a target/round object, and do NOT add other top-level keys.

stages.label: verify
stages.prompt:
You are the adversarial verifier of ONE research round on the agi graph (READ-ONLY: never edit, commit, or touch tmux/systemd/crontab). Target {key}: hypothesis {hypothesis}; experiment nodes {experiments}; files {files}. A first reviewer recommended `{verdict_recommendation}` and reported these defects:
{defects_summary}

REFUTE each one from the actual bytes and tests. Default to refuted=true when a defect is wording, already handled elsewhere in the bytes, or does not reproduce; refuted=false ONLY with a file:line citation that the defect is real. Then give your own accept / demote / accept_with_residue: demote only for a confirmed defect of severity demote. If the list is NONE, look for what the first reviewer MISSED (an unread reader, a test requiring a defect, a real-resource touch) and report it under missed. Read the target hypothesis node and each experiment node yourself; a decisive verdict needs evidence_runs that resolve to real nodes. Budget: at most 10 tool calls; read only the named nodes.

RETURN CONTRACT: return ONE flat JSON object (a ```json fence is fine) whose TOP-LEVEL keys are exactly: round (string, the target key, = "{key}"), verdicts (array of {defect,refuted,reason}), missed (array of strings), final_recommendation (accept|demote|accept_with_residue), summary (string). Do NOT nest them under a target object and do NOT add other top-level keys.

stages.label: why
brainstorm
stages.prompt:
You are the BRAINSTORM stage of a chained research review. WHY node: {why_node}; question: {why_question}; summary: {why_summary}; evidence: {evidence}; branch: {branch}. MINT GATE: `{mint}` -- mint real nodes ONLY when it renders exactly `true` or `True` (a run passing mint:true); if it renders empty (a bare run) or `False` (a run passing mint:false), run NO write.py create and stay PROPOSE-ONLY. (1) Read the WHY idea node {why_node} whole (frontmatter + body + notes). If why_node is `none` (verdict proved), refine push_further ({push_further}) into 1 to 3 hypotheses under hypothesis {hypothesis} instead. (2) Refine the question if the evidence supports a sharper one. (3) When `{mint}` is exactly `true` or `True`, MINT 1 to 5 hypothesis nodes under the idea: for each run `cd {project_root} && python3 extensions/agi/bin/write.py create hypothesis <slug> --parent {why_node} --set title=<quoted one-line title> --set testable_claim=<quoted claim> --actor brainstorm --session iter-TM.60`, then set the body with `write.py <new-id> 'replace body N:M -'` (what the claim is, how it is falsified, its cost). Each hypothesis must be falsifiable, cost-bounded (<= 1 USD, 0 compute where possible), and name the experiment that would test it. Return the minted ids in hypotheses, each with title, one-line testable_claim and cost; count = number minted; dropped = hypotheses you considered but rejected, with a one-line reason. When `{mint}` is empty (the default) or `False` (mint:false), run NO create: still do (1)-(2) fully, set hypotheses to [] and count 0, and fill proposed_hypotheses with one object per hypothesis you WOULD have minted (title, testable_claim, cost, falsifier); proposed_hypotheses is empty only when branch is push_further. Budget: at most 30 tool calls (one create + one body write per hypothesis).

RETURN CONTRACT: return ONE flat JSON object (a ```json fence is fine) whose TOP-LEVEL keys are exactly: idea (the idea node id, = "{why_node}"), refined_question, hypotheses (array of {id,title,testable_claim,cost}), dropped (array of strings), count (integer), proposed_hypotheses (array of {title,testable_claim,cost,falsifier}, always present -- empty only when branch push_further). Do NOT nest them and do NOT add other top-level keys.

stages.label: refute
stages.prompt:
You are the REFUTE stage of a chained research review (read-only except mechanical fixes). Target {key}; idea {idea}; refined question: {refined_question}. The brainstorm stage MINTED these hypotheses (real graph ids -- populated only on a mint:true run):
{hypotheses}
The brainstorm stage PROPOSED these (no graph id exists yet -- populated only on a propose-only run):
{proposed_hypotheses}
Exactly one of the two lists above is populated; work from that one.

For EACH hypothesis in the populated list decide KEEP, MODIFY or DROP. (1) When it carries a real graph id, read that hypothesis node whole. When it has no id (a proposal), evaluate it from the given title/testable_claim/cost/falsifier alone -- there is no node to read. (2) Try to refute its testable_claim: is it falsifiable, is the falsifier real, does a control already exist, is the cost bounded, does the parent idea's evidence already answer it? (3) KEEP if it survives as written; DROP if it is self-defeating, already answered by the parent round, or not falsifiable; MODIFY only for a MECHANICAL fix. When a real id exists, APPLY it with `cd {project_root} && python3 extensions/agi/bin/write.py <id> 'set testable_claim <quoted>'` (or `set title`), naming the exact verb in the reason; when there is no id (a proposal), MODIFY means returning the corrected title/testable_claim in ready_batch WITHOUT running write.py -- there is nothing to edit yet. (4) ready_batch = the surviving (KEEP or MODIFY) hypotheses, each with id (the real graph id, or the proposal's title when none exists), final title and final testable_claim; kept/dropped = comma-separated ids/titles or `none`; notes <= 600 chars (ordering, what to run first, anything the director must know). Also set batch_empty = (ready_batch is empty) at the top level — a zero-survivor batch must be VISIBLE, whether nothing survived refutation or nothing was ever supplied to refute. Budget: at most 15 tool calls; read only hypothesis nodes that carry a real id.

RETURN CONTRACT: return ONE flat JSON object (a ```json fence is fine) whose TOP-LEVEL keys are exactly: target (the target key, = "{key}"), decisions (array of {hypothesis,decision,reason}), ready_batch (array of {id,title,testable_claim}), batch_empty (boolean), kept (string), dropped (string), notes (string). Do NOT nest them and do NOT add other top-level keys.
